segments.text: Goosebumps are completely useless. Well, that's not exactly true. They're a leftover from when our ancestors were much hairier.
Every hair on your body has a tiny muscle attached to it. When you're cold, those muscles pull, and the hair stands up.
For furry animals, that trick is great. Raised fur traps a layer of warm air, like a puffy jacket.
Here's the wild part. It also makes animals look bigger. That's why a scared cat puffs up its tail.
In fact, the same alarm system fires when you feel strong emotions. That's why a great song can give you chills.
That's not all. Scientists found the same muscle and nerve also help wake up the cells that grow new hair.
So goosebumps aren't useless. They're your inner fur, still trying to keep you warm.
